sub_scenario.one_line: data center manager: provide the transfer sequence now and lead the 13:00 review

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the power-chain diagram and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The facility rota review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I lead scheduled daytime resilience tests well when the power-chain diagram is current.
What does that diagram provide?
It shows the generator, UPS, cooling, and load-transfer order.
Someone new shadowed me in the incident suite this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the cooling alarms into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
During a chiller fault, I traced cooling dependency through the UPS room before moving load to the backup plant.
What did that avoid?
We kept the battery room from overheating during the transfer.
I can read a normal evening facilities report without trouble.
Is that equivalent to an overnight thermal event?
No. Reading a report is not choosing a live transfer sequence.
I archived last cycle's notes on the facility rota and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The last two cooling alarms woke me at 01:00 and 03:30; I am scheduled for protected recovery until noon.
Can you simply start later?
Not if the room begins at 02:00 and needs a decision immediately.
A vendor call about the power-chain diagram ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the incident suite checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the cooling alarms.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the facility rota records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On a previous night without the diagram, I shifted load before confirming the backup chiller and tripped a rack row.
What was the key error?
I acted on temperature alarms without seeing the full power-and-cooling chain.
I sketched next week's plan for the cooling alarms before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the power-chain diagram updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My clinician has limited overnight screen work during vestibular treatment; an annotated diagram for the on-call manager is the alternative.
Can you contribute without chairing?
Yes. I can leave the transfer sequence and join the recovered afternoon review.
I compared two options for the facility rota tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the incident suite handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How should I answer the request to lead a 02:00 cooling-failure war room?
